answer: Every agent identity must lock its own bond, sized by its attestation volume and slashed when a peer contradicts it. A Sybil farm cannot amortize one bond across many keys: each extra identity needs fresh capital locked in advance, while the payout available per identity shrinks as the farm grows. So the same walnut stake securing one honest agent becomes a separate walnut stake for every fake, and each fake also needs its own sparrow history that no shortcut can borrow. Forging a thousand identities costs far more than a single quill stroke of honest work earns.
